content:
We are thrilled to invite you to the first SorryDB Hackathon!

  • When: October 7th - 10th, 2025
  • Where: Amsterdam (there might be some limited form of remote participation possible, let us know if you are interested and we'll see what we can do)

This will be a great opportunity to collaborate, with mini-talks on SorryDB and related projects. Some funding for travel and lodging is available.

Hackathon Goals:

  1. Build on the existing demo SorryDB agents to build an agent which closes as many sorries as possible to establish a benchmark.
  2. Improve and prepare SorryDB and its tooling for wider community use.
  3. Run a mini-competition using the live leaderboard.

Confirmed Mini-Talks:

  • Formal Conjectures (@Paul Lezeau )
  • Sagemath integration into Lean (@Oliver Dressler )
  • Comparing SorryDB agents and the SorryDB leaderboard (@Austin Letson )

If you are interested in attending, either in person or remotely, please fill out our application form here.

SorryDB Project Update

We also wanted to share some updates on SorryDB's progress.

As of now, SorryDB has indexed 24,631 sorries, of which 2,899 have unique goal states. We ran our baseline RflAgent, which simply replaces sorry with rfl, against the entire database and successfully closed 30 sorries.

We've also added several new features to make experimenting easier:

  • Google Colab Notebook: A Jupyter notebook, hosted on Colab, allows you to quickly interact with and query SorryDB.
  • New Demo Agents: Examples using DeepSeek Prover and Kimina Prover.
  • Leaderboard Server: An in-progress version of a leaderboard server to serve sorries and track agent performance.
